title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 293ff of 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'): X is a Riemann surface with a finite set X^! of marked points carrying multiplicities d_X, i.e. an orbifold (X,d_X). A finite group 𝒢 acts on it, possibly with antiholomorphic elements. G = 𝒢^+ is the holomorphic subgroup, Y = X/G, and H = 𝒢/G. The previous page states the corollary: for x in U = X∖X^! with image y in V = Y∖Y^!, there is a canonical isomorphism π1((X,d_X,𝒢),x) ≅ π1((Y,d_Y,H),y) of equivariant orbifold fundamental groups. Elements of the left side are classes of pairs (γ,l), with γ∈𝒢 and l a path class in U from x to γ^{-1}x. Pairs are taken modulo the normal subgroup generated by the λ_a^{d_X(a)}.

This page makes the isomorphism explicit. The image β of α=[(γ,l)] is (γ̇, f_U(l)), where γ̇ is the image of γ in H and f_U(l) is a path class in V from y=f_U(x) to γ̇^{-1}y = f_U(γ^{-1}x). Well-definedness: π1(f_U,x): π1(U,x) → π1(V,y) sends a loop λ_a around a∈X^! to (a conjugate of) λ_b^{ν(a)}. Here b=f(a) and ν(a)=|G_a| is the ramification index. Hence λ_a^{d_X(a)} goes to λ_b^{d_X(a)ν(a)} = λ_b^{d_Y(b)}, so the defining relations are respected.

The page then returns to the example (13):
- X = U_{0,3}^an = P^1∖{0,1,∞}.
- 𝒢 = T_{0,3} = S_3 × Z/2, the full group of conformal and anticonformal automorphisms; G = T_{0,3}^+ = S_3.
- Marked set X^! = {2,−1,1/2; −j,−j^2}: the points with nontrivial S_3-stabilizer.
- Y ≅ P^1∖{0}, Y^! = {1,∞}, H = Z/2 (complex conjugation).
- The quotient map P^1 → P^1 is f(z) = (3^3/2^2) z^2(z−1)^2/(z^2−z+1)^3, which is 1728/j(λ) for the Legendre λ-to-j map.

Check of f:
- f(0)=f(1)=f(∞)=0.
- f(2)=f(−1)=f(1/2)=1, each with index 2.
- The roots of z^2−z+1, namely −j and −j^2, go to ∞ with index 3.
- The degree is 6 = |S_3|.

With d_X trivial, d_Y(1)=2 and d_Y(∞)=3. Then π1(Y,d_Y) = Z/2*Z/3 ≅ PSL_2(Z), and with the Z/2 extension one gets PGL_2(Z), the 'triangulated non-oriented cartographic group' π̃'_{0,3} of the next page. The corollary thus realises PGL_2(Z) as an extension of S_3×Z/2 by π1(U_{0,3}) = F_2 (cf. Γ(2)/±1 free, PSL_2(Z)/Γ(2) ≅ S_3). The purpose is to fix explicit generators and base points (next page: y=−j̄, triangles, arcs through 2, −1, 1/2) for loop computations.
errors: Minor imprecision: π1(f_U,x) sends λ_a to a conjugate of λ_b^{ν(a)} (the conjugator depends on path choices), not literally to λ_b^{ν(a)}; harmless since only normal subgroups matter.
'f_u(l) est un chemin de chemin' is a slip for 'une classe de chemins'.
ν(a)=[G_a] should be read as the order of the stabilizer in the holomorphic subgroup G=𝒢^+, not in 𝒢; otherwise d_Y(b)=d_X(a)ν(a) would fail for points fixed by antiholomorphic elements.

ideas.what: Equivariant orbifold fundamental group π1(X,d_X,𝒢;x) built from pairs (γ, path x→γ^{-1}x) modulo λ_a^{d_X(a)}, and its invariance under passing to the quotient by the holomorphic subgroup
ideas.modern_name: orbifold fundamental group of a global quotient / fundamental group of the quotient stack [U/𝒢] with root structure; Haefliger–Thurston orbifold covering theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thurston (orbifolds, 1978), Haefliger; classical Fuchsian group theory
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche (1981); not this explicit formula as far as known

ideas.what: Explicit S_3-quotient map f(z)=27/4·z^2(z−1)^2/(z^2−z+1)^3 of P^1∖{0,1,∞}, branched over 1 (index 2) and ∞ (index 3)
ideas.modern_name: 1728/j(λ), the Legendre λ ↦ j map; identification PGL_2(Z) ≅ (F_2 ⋊ S_3)⋊Z/2
ideas.where_published: Cartographic groups C_2 and their relation to PSL_2/PGL_2(Z) appear in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Non-oriented triangulated cartographic group π̃'_{0,3} identified with the equivariant π1 including antiholomorphic involution
ideas.modern_name: extended modular group PGL_2(Z) as orbifold π1 of the real-structure quotient; cartographic groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §2-3 on cartographic groups

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but standard verification in orbifold covering theory, plus the classical λ↦j quotient map, set up to fix base points for later loop computations. Nothing here appears new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Opening likely reads 'canoniques, dont l'image β des α ∈ π1(X,d_X,𝒢;x) définis par (γ,l) dans π1(Y,d_Y,ℋ;y) est (γ̇, f_U(l))'; '295' is Grothendieck's own page number.
'un = α' / 'un = β' should read 'un même α' / 'un même β'.
'f_u(l) est un chemin de chemin' is likely 'une classe de chemins'.
'vérifie que' is crossed out and replaced by 'envoie'; the passage reads 'envoie un λ_a dans un λ_b^{ν(a)}'.
Margin insertion: X^! = {2, −1, 1/2; −j, −j^2} (an earlier entry crossed out); 'G = T_{0,3}^+ = S_3' with 𝒢 = T_{0,3} = S_3 × Z/2.
